scope: Corollary 3.9 (Conditional geometric estimates in the limit) of the manuscript “Thermal FK–Ising interfaces and massive SLE” (preprints/Thermal-FK-Ising-interfaces-and-massive-SLE-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 223 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 c2a2a4a8b4213752), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 14. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Every limit of Proposition 3.7 inherits the conditional crossing estimates needed below in its natural driving filtration. They hold after a live stopping time and after localization on a finite interval on which the relevant Loewner coordinates remain nondegenerate. In the following two estimates, reset capacity time to zero at the chosen live stopping time. 1. In the current half-plane chart, put the tip at 0, rescale a given live point to modulus 1, and write x for its real part. If its imaginary part is small, so x is near 1 or −1, then P{the future trace visits B(x, d) | past} ≤ Kdα for all sufficiently small d. 2. For a live physical point w, P  inf s before swallowing cradOs (w) < ε cradO0 (w) past at the restart  ≤ Kεα . The assertions apply in particular at inverse elapsed-clock times and at first angular-level crossings used in Section 4. No semimartingale property of the driver is assumed here.
